author: Greg Oshust
title: Griffin becoming a big-play option for Pebblebrook - NewsBreak
text:
By Greg Oshust ,
1 days ago Pebblebrook’s Demitri Griffen is becoming a big-play target in the Falcons' offense. By Anthony Stalcup Demitri Griffin has emerged as a go-to guy on offense for Pebblebrook this season.
The sophomore wide receiver will try to help lead the Falcons to victory when they go on the road to take on rival Campbell in a crucial Region 3 game for both teams at Richard McDaniel Stadium.
Griffin has displayed a big-play capability for Pebblebrook (2-3, 0-1) with eight receptions for 157 yards and three touchdowns, catching three passes for 107 yards and two scores in the Falcons’ 50-3 victory over Riverwood on Sept. 10.
Griffin, who had 39 receptions for 605 yards and four touchdowns and was an All-Region 3 selection as a freshman last year, has already attracted recruiting attention, with Georgia State making the sophomore standout an offer last month.
“He’s a big play guy – he’s a guy who can do it all,” Pebblebrook coach Rodney Hackney said. “He’s a possession receiver and also has the speed to challenge you deep., so we use him in different ways. He’s also a punter right now for us as well, so he does it all. He has a great family. Demetri comes in a does a tremendous job for us. He had a good freshman year, made all-region last year. His dad does a great job of helping train him and we just kind of build on those things. Demetri is a top-notch guy. He’s one of our best players and we depend on him a lot for big plays and stuff like that throughout the game.”
Griffin will be one of the key players Pebblebrook will rely on, along with sophomore quarterback Matthew Benton, junior wide receiver Tyree Carter and junior linebacker Necho Benton, as the Falcons try to keep their state playoff hopes alive and maintain the momentum they built in a close 35-28 loss to Hillgrove two weeks ago.
“They do a good job over at Campbell,” Hackney said. “They beat us last year (21-7), but we didn’t play our kind of ball that we should have played., so we’re definitely looking at it from a different standpoint. We’ve got to go into it with a different focus this year. We know it’s a new game, a new season. We’re looking ahead to make sure that we take care of business and we’re up for the challenge and we know that it’s at their place, so they will have a small advantage that way as well. But we’re looking forward to the challenge. We played well the second half against Hillgrove, so if we can keep that same momentum against Campbell, we’ll be OK.”
It’s also an important game for Campbell (1-3) as it tries to bounce back with a win in its region opener after three straight losses – including a 53-0 defeat at the hands of Marist two weeks ago –and keep itself in the postseason hunt as well.
“It’s very important,” Campbell coach Jeff Phillips said. “It’s a rival game and you want to stay alive to have a chance of making it to the postseason, so it’s something to keep your program going in the right direction.”
Campbell looks to have senior quarterback Davin Lemire, who was injured early in the Spartans’ 29-0 loss to North Forsyth and hasn’t played since, back in the lineup, with junior wide receiver Pierre Mendy and senior strong safety Cortez Stephens also playing key roles.
